projects.title: PuffLite: An Object-Storage-Native Search Engine with LSM Compaction
projects.pitch: Build a tiny turbopuffer-style search service whose source of truth is S3-compatible object storage (MinIO). Writes land in a WAL, get flushed to immutable segment files with a BM25 inverted index and an IVF vector index, and a background compactor merges segments. Queries combine text and vector results and are served from a local NVMe/memory cache tier in front of cold object storage.
stack: Parquet or a custom segment format
you_will_learn: LSM-tree write path: WAL, memtable, immutable segments, compaction
Inverted index construction and BM25 scoring
Approximate nearest neighbor indexing (IVF) and recall/latency tradeoffs
Tiered caching over high-latency object storage
Read-after-write consistency when the store is eventually listed
Write amplification vs. read amplification measurement
milestones: WAL + memtable that flushes to immutable segment objects on MinIO with a manifest file updated via conditional PUT
Per-segment BM25 inverted index and a query path that fans out across segments
Add IVF vector index per segment and hybrid ranking (reciprocal rank fusion)
Background compactor that merges small segments and atomically swaps the manifest; measure write/read amplification
Local disk cache with LRU eviction and prefetch; plot p50/p99 cold vs. warm query latency

projects.title: Backpressure Lab: A Mini Serverless Event Stream with Consumer Groups
projects.pitch: Recreate the core idea behind Cloudflare K2: decouple producers and consumers in scale and time. Build a single-node append-only log broker with partitions, consumer groups, committed offsets, and explicit backpressure (credit-based flow control), then hammer it with a load generator to watch what happens when consumers fall behind.
stack: Append-only segmented log files with mmap
you_will_learn: Log-structured storage and segment rotation/retention
Partitioning and ordering guarantees per key
At-least-once delivery, offset commits, and idempotent consumers
Credit-based flow control vs. buffering vs. load shedding
Consumer lag as an observability signal
milestones: Single-partition append-only log with fsync policy options and segment rotation
Multiple partitions with key-hash routing and per-partition ordering
Consumer groups with committed offsets and rebalancing when consumers join/leave
Credit-based backpressure on the push path; compare against unbounded buffering under a 10x producer spike
Dashboard showing throughput, consumer lag, and redelivery counts; write up a failure-injection report (kill consumer mid-batch)

projects.title: System-1 Router: A Low-Latency Decision Model Gateway with LoRA Hot-Swapping
projects.pitch: Serve a small open decision model (like jeff's 0.8B base) behind a gateway that picks between options with calibrated probabilities, hot-swaps LoRA adapters per domain, and micro-batches requests to hit millisecond latency targets. Use it as a router: cheap fast model decides, expensive LLM only called when confidence is low.
stack: vLLM or llama.cpp with LoRA support
you_will_learn: Dynamic micro-batching and the latency vs. throughput tradeoff
Adapter caching: LRU of LoRA weights in GPU/CPU memory
Probability calibration (ECE, reliability diagrams, temperature scaling)
Confidence-based cascading / fallback architecture
Tail-latency tracing with distributed spans
milestones: Run the base model locally and expose a /decide endpoint returning option probabilities
Add a LoRA adapter registry with LRU cache and measure swap cost (cold vs. warm adapter)
Implement a micro-batcher with max-wait and max-batch knobs; graph p50/p99 vs. QPS
Measure calibration on a labeled set, apply temperature scaling, show reliability diagrams before/after
Build the cascade: escalate to a large LLM below a confidence threshold, and report cost/accuracy curves

projects.title: Hotspot Daily: A Self-Hosted Trend Aggregator with Dedup and Idempotent Pipelines
projects.pitch: Build your own AIHOT-style industry digest: ingest RSS, GitHub trending, and HN on a schedule, dedupe near-identical stories, rank them with your own criteria, and generate a daily report. The engineering focus is making the pipeline idempotent, resumable, and politely rate-limited rather than just calling an LLM.
stack: A local LLM via Ollama for summaries
you_will_learn: Idempotent ingestion with content hashes and upserts
Near-duplicate detection with SimHash/MinHash and LSH bucketing
Job queues with retries, exponential backoff, and dead-letter queues
Per-source rate limiting with token buckets and ETag/If-Modified-Since caching
Exactly-once-ish effects via outbox pattern for report publishing
milestones: Fetchers for 3 sources with conditional GET caching and token-bucket rate limits
Normalized items table with content-hash upserts so reruns are safe
SimHash + LSH dedup clustering stories across sources; evaluate precision on a hand-labeled sample
Scoring stage with pluggable criteria and an LLM summarizer behind a queue with DLQ
Daily report generation via an outbox table; kill the worker mid-run and prove no duplicate reports

projects.title: Fail-Static SDK: Reproducing the Firebase Crash and Building a Kill-Switch Config Service
projects.pitch: The Firebase outage crashed client apps because of a backend change. Build a remote-config service plus a client SDK that cannot take down its host app: schema-validated configs, staged rollouts, last-known-good caching, and a circuit breaker. First reproduce the failure mode, then engineer it away.
you_will_learn: Fail-static vs. fail-closed design for client SDKs
Versioned configs, schema validation, and safe deserialization
Staged/percentage rollouts with automatic rollback on error-rate SLO breach
Circuit breakers, timeouts, and last-known-good caching
Blast-radius reduction and incident observability
milestones: Naive config server + SDK; reproduce a crash by shipping a malformed payload
Add schema validation on publish and defensive parsing with last-known-good fallback in the SDK
Versioned configs with percentage rollouts keyed on stable client hash
Client-side telemetry and server-side auto-rollback when error rate exceeds threshold
Chaos run with Toxiproxy (latency, garbage responses, outage) and a written postmortem showing zero host crashes
